data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on Popper's terms as a non-inductive, methodological decision to act on the theory that has withstood the most severe attempts at falsification, accepting the cost that this preference offers no guarantee of future success or truth-likeness, only a record of past survival.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the agent requires a probabilistic guarantee of success before acting, this defense fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'severe testing' implicitly assumes the uniformity of nature to define severity, the non-inductive claim collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Methodological Decisionism: The preference is not a logical inference about probability but a pragmatic rule of action. We choose the corroborated theory because it is the only one not yet known to be false, and acting on a known falsehood is irrational. This avoids induction by treating the preference as a volitional commitment to the aim of science (truth) rather than a prediction derived from past regularity.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
